chunks: He said: Abu 'Ali al-Hasan ibn Abdillah al-Qattan reported to me from Abu Amru Uthman ibn Ahmad, known as Ibn al-Sammak, who reported from Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Salih al-Tammar, who reported from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Razi, who reported from Abdullah ibn Raja, who reported from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Habshi ibn Junadah, who said:

I was once sitting with Abu Bakr when a man came to him and said: "O Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, indeed the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, promised to scoop for me three handfuls of dates." So Abu Bakr said: "Call 'Ali for me." Then 'Ali, peace be upon him, came, and Abu Bakr said: "O Abul Hasan, this man claims that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, promised him to scoop for him three handfuls of dates, so scoop them for him." So he scooped for him three handfuls of dates, and Abu Bakr said: "Count them." They found sixty dates in each handful.

Then Abu Bakr said: "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, spoke the truth. I heard him on the night of the Hijrah while we were departing from Makkah to Madinah, saying: 'O Abu Bakr, my palm and 'Ali's palm are equal in justice.'"

key_terms.الْهِجْرَة: Hijrah — the migration from Makkah to Madinah
key_terms.حَثَيَات: Handfuls — what is scooped with both palms together

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about his palm and Ali's palm on the night of Hijrah?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts how a man asked Abu Bakr to fulfill the Prophet's promise of three handfuls of dates. Abu Bakr called upon Ali to give them, and each handful contained exactly sixty dates, demonstrating the miraculous equivalence of the Prophet's and Ali's hands. Abu Bakr testified that on the night of Hijrah, the Prophet declared his palm and Ali's palm equal in justice.
